summary: Piscataquis County, Maine tower built in 1919 (sources give 42, 48 or 60 ft); said to have moved to Trout Mountain in 1931; the register lists the site as gone.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, with a watchman's camp and telephone built alongside
facts.status_note: Registered as removed and relocated to Trout Mountain in 1931; no source describes the site today

events.note: Steel tower erected; the 1919 annual report gives 48 ft, Maine History Online gives 60 ft, a newspaper item 42 ft
1920 inventory still lists a 48-foot steel tower
Station said to have moved to Trout Mountain; the Trout link appears in a caption beside a Black Cat photo, so it is probable, not proven
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three heights appear: 42 ft (August 1919 newspaper item), 48 ft (1919 annual report and 1920 inventory), 60 ft (Maine Memory 1920 caption and Maine History Online). We use 48 ft, the figure the state's own annual report gives, and flag the others.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 14.6 m matches the 48-ft figure. The Trout Mountain link rests on one Maine History Online caption; the Trout tower standing today was built in 2020 from Alabama parts and is not the Black Cat tower. No source found on staffing, fires or the site today.
